title: Constant diagrams preserve flat-term K-flat complexes with evaluated tensor normalization
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small Grothendieck site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $J$ a small category. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the ringed diagram site $\mathcal D=J^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C$ with ring $\Delta R$, constant-diagram functor $\Delta$, and exact evaluations $e_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. For any unbounded cochain complex $P$ of $R$-modules that is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $\Delta P$ is K-flat over $\Delta R$ and has flat terms. More precisely, for any complex $A$ of $\Delta R$-modules there are natural cochain isomorphisms
$$e_j\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_{\Delta R}\Delta P)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(e_jA\otimes_RP),$$
with the actual direct-sum total differentials [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], taking each local pure tensor $x\otimes p$ to $x\otimes p$. They are natural in $A$ and $P$. If $A$ is acyclic, these evaluated total tensors and the diagram total tensor are acyclic. The same normalization identifies evaluation of tensor by $\Delta P^i$ with tensor by $P^i$ on every exact sequence of diagrams. These assertions apply to every small site and every such $P$, including a localized site and an extended complex, without boundedness or a constant coefficient-ring hypothesis.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] to work in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(R))$. Each $e_j$ is additive and exact. A diagram $M$ is zero if and only if every $M(j)$ is zero: if all components vanish, the unique component maps $M(j)\to0$ and $0\to M(j)$ give inverse natural transformations. This also holds when $J$ is empty, since there is exactly one empty diagram and one morphism between any two empty diagrams. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to obtain $e_jH^n(B)\cong H^n(e_jB)$ for every complex $B$ and integer $n$. Thus $B$ is acyclic if and only if every $e_jB$ is acyclic. Exactness of a sequence of diagrams is likewise detected by evaluations, by applying the same cohomology comparison to the three-term complex of that sequence.

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor); agent application to the exact evaluations and zero detection of the diagram-site realization

proof.text: Evaluation preserves the direct sums needed below. Indeed, for any small family of diagrams $M_a$, form $S(j)=\bigoplus_aM_a(j)$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, with $S(\alpha)$ the unique map satisfying $S(\alpha)\iota_a=\iota_aM_a(\alpha)$. Identity and composition follow by equality on the coproduct inclusions. A family of natural transformations $M_a\to N$ induces unique maps $S(j)\to N(j)$; their naturality follows by equality on each $\iota_a$. This is exactly the coproduct universal property in the diagram category, and its evaluation is the coproduct universal property in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Transport this construction through [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. In particular the comparison $e_j(\bigoplus_{r+s=n}M_{r,s})\cong\bigoplus_{r+s=n}e_jM_{r,s}$ is the one preserving all the specified inclusions. The sums exist as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

source.place: Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits); explicit coproduct universal-property argument in the diagram category

proof.text: For each $j$, the inverse image on sets in [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] is evaluation and preserves finite limits; it is a left adjoint by the stated evaluation adjunction. The module evaluation with ring identification $e_j\Delta R=R$ is an algebraic inverse-image presentation [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]: all its operation comparisons are identities on the component ring and module operations. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] to this presentation. For arbitrary module diagrams $M,N$ this gives natural isomorphisms $\tau_{j,M,N}:e_j(M\otimes_{\Delta R}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}e_jM\otimes_Re_jN$ carrying an evaluated sheafified pure tensor to the pure tensor of its evaluated factors. These are the actual pairings of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Specializing $N=\Delta Q$, with $e_j\Delta Q=Q$ on objects and morphisms, gives $e_j(M\otimes_{\Delta R}\Delta Q)\cong(e_jM)\otimes_RQ$ with local formula $x\otimes q\mapsto x\otimes q$.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), algebraic inverse-image part; specialization to the evaluation geometric morphism

proof.text: In total degree $n$, combine Step 2 with the direct sum of the Step 3 comparisons for $(M,Q)=(A^r,P^s)$, $r+s=n$. This gives the required degreewise isomorphism. By [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] the differential on the $(r,s)$ summand is $d_A^r\otimes1+(-1)^r1\otimes d_P^s$. Naturality of $\tau$ in the two module variables identifies its two images respectively with $d_{e_jA}^r\otimes1$ and $(-1)^r1\otimes d_P^s$; evaluation preserves the sum and the integer sign because it is additive. Thus the degreewise isomorphisms commute with the actual total differentials and constitute a cochain isomorphism. Its inverse also commutes with differentials, by multiplying this cochain equation by the degreewise inverses. All comparisons preserve the $(r,s)$ inclusions and send $x\otimes p$ to $x\otimes p$.

source.place: Tag 06YL (section-flat), total tensor convention before Definition 06YN; homology.tex Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex); explicit signed differential calculation

proof.text: For cochain maps $a:A\to A^{\prime}$ and $b:P\to P^{\prime}$, on the $(r,s)$ coproduct inclusion the naturality square of Step 4 is precisely the naturality square of $\tau_{j,A^r,\Delta P^s}$ for $(a^r,\Delta b^s)$. Hence the square commutes by Step 3 and equality on coproduct inclusions. Its local formula is $x\otimes p\mapsto a^r(x)\otimes b^s(p)$ on either path, with no degree permutation or additional sign. The same module comparison, with $Q=P^i$, is natural for every arrow of an exact sequence of diagrams; it therefore identifies the evaluated tensor sequence with that sequence evaluated first and tensored with $P^i$.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), functoriality; homology.tex Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex), maps on total summands

proof.text: Let $0\to M^{\prime}\to M\to M^{\prime\prime}\to0$ be any short exact sequence of $\Delta R$-module diagrams. For each $j$ its evaluation is short exact, and tensoring that evaluated sequence with $P^i$ is exact by the assumed flatness of $P^i$ and [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Step 5 identifies it with evaluation of the original sequence tensored with $\Delta P^i$. Detection of exactness from Step 1 shows that the latter sequence is exact before evaluation as well. Since the sequence was arbitrary, [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] says exactly that $\Delta P^i$ is flat, for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); elementary exactness test through the normalized evaluation comparisons

proof.text: Let $A$ be an arbitrary acyclic complex of $\Delta R$-modules. Step 1 makes $e_jA$ acyclic. Since $P$ is K-flat, [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes $\operatorname{Tot}(e_jA\otimes_RP)$ acyclic. The cochain isomorphism of Step 4 and the cohomology comparison in Step 1 imply that every evaluation of $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_{\Delta R}\Delta P)$ is acyclic, hence that the total complex itself is acyclic. This is K-flatness of $\Delta P$ by the same definition, and also proves the more precise acyclicity assertion. There was no boundedness assumption: degree $n$ used the entire small coproduct indexed by $r+s=n$, rather than a finite sum or a product. The argument applies anew to any small localized site with its ring sheaf and any extended complex satisfying the two stated assumptions; it uses neither constant coefficients on the original site nor a preservation theorem for localization or extension.
